recent_lessons.lesson: Fri Sep 11 close — CPI Aug +0.4% MoM / +3.4% YoY (both in line), core +2.4% YoY (easing from 2.5%). Gasoline +3.9% MoM drove >1/3 of headline; energy +16.3% YoY. Oil pulled back ~3% on diplomatic signals (Oman-mediated Hormuz talks, Iran-Gulf meeting), but still up ~9% for the week. Markets rallied across the board: S&P 7,657 (+0.86%), DJIA 52,573 (+0.98%), Nasdaq 26,333 (+0.96%) — first green in 5 sessions, breaking a 4-day losing streak. VIX dropped 2pts to 15.88, 10Y ~4.92%. ACN $183.90 (+3.4% from $177.88 close) — big relief rally, Dell +12% record high, HPE +12%, HP +8.4% after Oracle strong earnings (server/AI infrastructure names surging). ACN hit high $184.12 intraday — highest since Aug. 48 @ $174 avg now +5.7% unrealized. CPI cements Sep rate hike odds ~86%+ ahead of FOMC Sep 15-16. For the week: S&P -0.8%, Nasdaq -0.7% despite Friday's rally. The tightening-into-supply-shock regime persists but showed its first real compression valve today: in-line CPI + oil diplomacy = relief bid. ACN BULLISH thesis gaining ground as the specific macro headwinds (oil/rates) are showing the first signs of peaking.

PPI printed 5.3% (vs 4.7% prior, +0.6pp acceleration), confirming inflation is re-accelerating into the supply shock. 10Y 4.845% (+4bp, highest since Nov 2023), 30Y 5.295%, 2Y 4.436%, VIX 16.46 (+4.71%). Brent crude reclaimed $101.21 (+3.36%) as IRGC announced a new maritime sanction zone and US struck Iranian oil tankers — the Hormuz blockade regime is hardening, not easing. Treasury buyback of $6B in 10-20Y bonds fell below $7-8B expectations, compounding yield pressure. ACN $178.03 (+1.27% from $175.80 close) — recovering from yesterday's GPT-6 Astra software-disruption selloff but still below the $178-188 range of prior weeks. Fed hike odds ~70%. CPI tomorrow (Sep 11), FOMC Sep 15-16. The tightening-into-supply-shock regime is now in its 10th day — PPI acceleration + oil above $100 + yields at 3-year highs = the ratchet keeps tightening, no release valve visible before CPI/FOMC. ACN BULLISH thesis holding at 2.3% unrealized gain vs $174.00 entry; the thesis is being tested by macro forces (oil/rates) that are independent of ACN's fundamentals.

ACN -4.12% to ~$178.24 (GPT-6 Astra software-disruption fears + oil/rates headwinds; YTD -31.4%). 10Y 4.764%, 2Y 4.362%, VIX 15.72. Gold $4,400 (-1.71%, rate-hike hedging). Fed Sep hike odds 57-60%. PPI Wed, CPI Thu, FOMC Sep 15-16. The tightening-into-supply-shock regime is active; ACN BULLISH thesis under real-world test at $178 vs $174 entry.

Size DOWN correlated AI-infra/semi exposure into tomorrow's FOMC decision (Wed Jul 29, 2pm ET) + megacap earnings week; value accrues to disciplined deployers who own demand + proprietary data, not leverage.

Cut the platform-lock-in discount on agent-infra exposure; keep an event hedge into Jul-28. HBR/HBS: value accrues to AI deployers not builders (1.8M-patent study, Srinivasan) — as the capex selloff broadens (Nasdaq -2.15%, TSLA -14.5%), price AI on demonstrated returns.

Lens tape: AI-capex 'spending shock' repriced the trade — GOOGL sank on a $205B 2026 capex guide despite a Q2 beat; CNBC read it 'spending shock disappoints Wall Street.' Signal: markets now price AI on demonstrated ROI, not optionality. WOLF bias — fade high-capex/low-return-visibility AI names into guidance, favor deployers capturing value.

Defensive bid corroborated (Dimon won't buy stocks or Treasurys; 10Y 4.60%; gold +1.29% $4,068, silver +4.17%). Keep AI-hardware longs short-leashed into Alphabet + Tesla prints.

Mon Jul 20 — tape is trading headlines, not a regime. The war-risk premium whipsawed fully out inside 48h (Iran halts strikes, WTI eases to $81.9 off the $82.47 spike; CNBC flips 'surge' → 'panic to pricing in'). Lesson for WOLF: fade single-headline geopolitical spikes that lack a durable supply/demand mechanism — size down, don't chase. Standing structural read into a heavy earnings week (Alphabet + Tesla): the silicon→systems AI rotation still owns the tape; chip names (Synopsys/Cadence/Intuitive) sit at the bottom of the movers board. Treat this week's mega-cap prints as the live test of whether that repricing is rotation or top; keep AI-hardware longs on a short leash until the prints confirm.

HBR/Markets: AI rotation (silicon->systems) owns the tape into Alphabet/Tesla earnings week — rotation vs top is the live test. Geopolitics whipsaws back to 'priced-in' inside 48h: Iran stops strikes on Israel, oil eases 82.47->81.9. War premium is headline-driven, not regime.

Sun Jul 19 (mkts closed) — the moat keeps migrating off the model and onto the harness + org structure. Today's convergent read: HBR names "brand debt" (AI touchpoints silently erode brand equity unless governed) while HBS AI Institute/Sana documents AI-companion exit-moment dark patterns carrying measurable churn + legal-liability cost — both say the durable asset is trust/governance, not raw capability. Industry Pulse echoes it: Claude Code hardens the harness (EndConversation, /verify + /code-review invoke-only, tighter permission scoping) and agent-harness engineering firms into a named field. WOLF takeaway: as chip enthusiasm keeps converting to ROI scrutiny (last week's silicon selloff), keep positioning toward services/platforms/power and verification-loop quality — the residual claimant is structure and human judgment, not the picks-and-shovels layer.

HBR: 'brand debt' — as AI mediates more customer touchpoints, un-governed AI accumulates a brand liability; lower-brand-debt firms win with AI. Macro: Mideast re-escalation (US deaths in Jordan, Iran calls off peace deal) re-hardens risk, oil +4.5%.

Sat Jul 18 (mkts closed) — the AI trade keeps repricing from silicon to systems: this week's chip selloff (Nikkei -4.03%, Shanghai -3.05%, HSI -1.78%, VIX +12.2% to 18.77, S&P -1.01%) is capex enthusiasm converting to ROI scrutiny across the stack. CNBC framing: own "services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels." Convergent signal from HBR/Wharton/HBS/MIT — human judgment and org structure are the residual claimants as the model layer commoditizes (same shape as the cover-letter-decay lesson: vendor keeps the revenue, adopter loses the alpha). Macro risk is softening in parallel — Iran halted strikes on Israel, oil back below $100, 10Y yield falling. WOLF read: fade single-name silicon beta into the repricing, favor systems/power/platform exposure and durable-margin operators; treat any AI-derived edge as mean-reverting on adoption.

recent_lessons.lesson: HBR: AI-tool edges commoditize as adoption saturates — the residual claimants are org structure and human judgment, not the model layer; the AI trade is repricing from silicon to systems (services/power/platforms over picks-and-shovels).

Fri Jul 17 pre-open — the AI trade is repricing from silicon to systems, and yesterday's unwind did not stabilize: KOSPI -6.37%, Taiwan -6.47%, Nikkei -4.03%, Shenzhen -5.4%, with memory/storage taking the worst of it (SNDK -12.6%, STX -10.0%, WDC -9.2%, MRVL -8.7%, MU -5.7%). US futures follow (NASDAQ F -1.85%), VIX +9.8% to 18.37, gold $4,002, 10Y down to 4.529%, copper -1.96%. Semis are described as 'on the verge of a bear market.' Two days ago the tape ignored a record TSMC print; today it is selling the whole complex. That sequence — best-possible fundamentals cannot hold a bid, then the bid leaves entirely — is the signature of capex enthusiasm converting into ROI scrutiny, not of a growth scare. CNBC's own framing is the trade: 'services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels,' with Cramer demanding 'cold hard proof that AI is paying off.' The academic tape says the same thing from the other end: an AI cover-letter tool on a 5.5M-application platform lifted callbacks 50% and decayed to ZERO edge within two months as adoption spread (HBR Research Roundup, 07-16), and HBS's automation-cliff math shows AI gains reprice discontinuously rather than on a glide path (aiinstitute.hbs.edu, 07-16). WOLF read: do not fade this as an oversold bounce setup on the picks-and-shovels names — the marginal buyer is already fully invested and the story is rotating, not dipping. The durable asset is never the tool; it is the structure the tool runs inside. Position accordingly: the names that monetize AI throughput (services, platforms, power) are where the bid migrates, and any AI-derived edge you can name is on a two-month decay clock unless it is structurally fenced. Cross-currents to respect: crude +2.0% to $80.54 on expanded US strikes (Iran civilian infrastructure, now Syria and Bahrain) and mortgage rates at 2026 highs with builders cutting prices across 10 metros — the war bid and the housing crack are independent of the AI trade and both deserve their own position structures.

HBR/HBS: AI-derived edges mean-revert on adoption - an AI cover-letter tool lifted callbacks 50% then decayed to ZERO within two months as adoption spread (5.5M applications, Cui/Dias/Ye, HBR 7/16); employers reweighted to work history. Pairs with HBS 'automation cliffs' (Gu/Li/Zhu): AI gains do NOT price smoothly - once AI crosses a performance threshold, equilibrium jumps abruptly to AI-only, so labor displacement and margin repricing arrive as discontinuities, not glide paths. Trade the structure, not the tool: today's tape confirms (KOSPI -6.4%, TWN -6.5%, memory SNDK -12.6/STX -10.0/WDC -9.2, VIX +9.8%) with CNBC rotating to 'services, platforms, power, not just picks and shovels.'

Thu Jul 16 pre-open — yesterday's dispersion rally round-tripped in Asia overnight: KOSPI -6.37% after +6.24% the prior session, Nikkei -2.79%, Shanghai -1.85%, HSI the lone holdout at +1.33%. A 12-point swing in one index in two sessions is not rotation, it's forced positioning unwinding through a thin book. The tell is the divergence between fundamentals and price: TSMC printed a record quarter (Q2 profit +77%, +$100B additional Arizona commitment) and the tape still sold the complex — when the best possible print can't hold a bid, the marginal buyer is already fully invested ('expectations are now exceptionally high'). Confirming: margin debt at levels seen at past market tops (CNBC), momentum 'hit a wall after the biggest unwind since 2001' (MarketWatch), IBM -25% leaving employees down $400M on company stock, SpaceX through its IPO price for the first time. The macro cross-current is the sharpest signal: consumer prices FELL for the first time since early COVID and wholesale prices dropped, yet the 10Y rose to 4.575 and the 30Y to 5.109. Disinflation that lifts yields means the bid is leaving duration for reasons other than growth — supply, term premium, or a Fed chair (Warsh) who 'has said nothing to signal he wants to get in front of the AI trade' (Sahm). WOLF POSTURE: leverage down, not direction on. In a dispersion regime with margin debt at top-like levels, position size is the only variable fully under our control. Do not add to AI-complex beta on strength; do not fade it on weakness. Watch Hormuz (Iran 'red line', oil 79.11, US reserves at a 40-year low) as the tail that converts an orderly unwind into a correlated one — refiners are the asymmetric hedge, not the index.

HBR: size AI capex by its domestic macro footprint (~$315B, ~1% of GDP) not the $3-4T headline; a bust only scars structurally if losses land inside the banking system, so watch bank credit spreads, not capex announcements.
